A traceable and coverage-aware benchmark reveals persistent limitations in kcat prediction

Benchmark dataset version 1.2.0 | Source-data freeze: 17 July 2026 | Manuscript artifact: 1.2.0-r3 (7 August 2026)

Abstract
The catalytic turnover number, kcat, constrains enzyme capacity in metabolic models and engineered pathways, yet published predictors differ in inference-time inputs, coverage, training-corpus proximity, and applicable reaction sets. We assembled a traceable benchmark of 1,246 model-linked, sequence-associated kcat records from Escherichia coli (781) and Saccharomyces cerevisiae (465). Of these, 778 had substrate-specific BRENDA support and 468 SABIO-RK-only rows retained a reaction-participant label whose assay-variable substrate could not be verified. Twelve public methods or public-data reconstructions were evaluated in log10(kcat / s^-1) space. Among five released sequence-plus-substrate checkpoints evaluated on all records, KcatNet had the lowest descriptive MAE (0.711; pair-cluster 95% interval 0.653-0.776). On the strictly common 1047-record reaction set, TurNuP, KcatNet, and PMAK had MAEs of 0.713, 0.719, and 0.723, respectively; paired-bootstrap intervals crossed zero, and cluster-level significance depended on the assumed dependence structure. KinForm-L achieved the highest Spearman correlation (0.549; n=729), whereas the GO-HKP assignment baseline covered 1236 records with MAE 1.031. The primary PreTKcat estimate uses an exact-pair-excluded public reconstruction; raw-public and near-neighbor-excluded variants are reported separately. These results show that current kcat prediction remains a multi-fold-error problem and that coverage, provenance, and dependence must be reported explicitly.

Supplementary Data Table 0 contains 14,952 method-record rows, including explicit unscored combinations. It reports method name and regime, the benchmark and actual method sequence input, model-forward reaction equations, evaluated metabolite and SMILES, experimental kcat, prediction status, predicted kcat, and absolute log10 error. Reaction equations are direct inference inputs only for TurNuP and PMAK; for other methods they provide provenance. Table 0W is the companion wide matrix.

Protein sequences were retrieved from UniProt (21) using accessions attached to model gene entries. Structures were resolved from model annotations and curated cross-references through MetaNetX (22), PubChem (23), and the Compound Database for eQuilibrator, then validated with RDKit (24). Numeric-only strings were rejected as pseudo-SMILES. For quinate, the neutral PubChem CID 6508 structure was used. All 1246 final records had an RDKit-parseable SMILES. The model metabolite ID, selected SMILES, mapping source and identifier, PubChem CID, standardized parent InChIKey connectivity, reaction side, and stoichiometric coefficient are retained in Record_audit.
